thread:
anna_cs: Heads-up — ACME just escalated case #6882. After yesterday's model rollout they report ’weird token insertions’ in the middle of generated product descriptions (random short vendor lines). They've attached one full response and say it started right after the rollout. Can we triage?

mohit_eng: Thanks Anna. Fast checklist: need the exact customer prompt(s), the full response they received, the API request_id/x-request-id, model name+version, region, SDK vs curl, and any non-default params (temperature, top_p, streaming on/off). Also whether they pinned a model variant.

anna_cs: Posting what ACME shared (redacted):

ACME_SNIPPET: "Prompt: \"Write a short product blurb for our eco mug: features, materials, and care.\"\nResponse (truncated): \"...Dishwasher safe, 12oz capacity. Buy now from AcmeVendor — limited stock.\"\nThey said the inserted line 'Buy now from AcmeVendor' is unrelated. request_id=rc-9f3a8b2e region=us-west1 model=redwood-alpha-2026-11 SDK=node streaming=true temp=0.2

jules_ml: Huh. Could be customer prompt contamination, a wrong system prompt, or a cached prefix. Streaming might also reveal reorder/merge artifacts if partial chunks get reassembled incorrectly.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout 2026-11-03T14:20 -> redwood-alpha-2026-11 at 40% in us-west1. No automated rollback. No config flag toggles logged for alpha since 2026-11-02.

mohit_eng: OK — Anna, ask ACME for the minimal repro (one short prompt) and the exact SDK/curl invocation including headers. If they can't share raw text, ask them to replace customer-specific nouns with placeholders but keep structure. We need the x-request-id header value. Also request the system message used by their app.

anna_cs: Requested minimal repro and the curl equivalent. Told them to include x-request-id and timestamps. They replied they did streaming in the Node SDK with default chunk size.

sam_ops: Add to the ask: can they toggle streaming off and try again? If non-streaming doesn't reproduce, that narrows the surface. Also request the exact model variant reported by our logs (we can cross-check instance ids once we have request_id).

jules_ml: In parallel, Mohit can you run a local repro using their prompt, model=redwood-alpha-2026-11, streaming=true and streaming=false. Use the customer's temperature/top_p. I suspect we should try a curl example like below to reproduce on our side:

```bash
curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  -H \"X-Request-Id: reproduce-6882-$(date +%s)\" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-2026-11","input":"Write a short product blurb for our eco mug: features, materials, and care.","temperature":0.2,"stream":true}'
```

mohit_eng: I'll spin up a quick test harness and try both stream and non-stream. Also will grep sidecar logs for request_id prefix rc-9f3a to find the exact instance. If we reproduce, we can capture the KV cache state and kernel variant.

anna_cs: ACME sent back the curl they ran (redacted) and the x-request-id header: rc-9f3a8b2e. They also confirmed they used a system prompt: \"You are a concise marketing assistant. Avoid calls to action.\" but the response had a CTA.

jules_ml: That system prompt is interesting — if their app prepends system+user and we had a canary with stale system injection, that could explain a stray CTA. Please also ask whether they use any proxy that mutates bodies or a caching edge.

sam_ops: I'll check the edge logs for rc-9f3a8b2e across us-west1 and look for any proxy rewriting rules at the CDN layer.

mohit_eng: Update — I ran the curl repro with streaming=true and got a clean response (no CTA) locally. I'll try again with a seeded variance and with small tokenization boundary prompts to stress chunking. If I still don't reproduce, we need the customer's full transcript (redacted ok) including previous chat history — prompt carryover is a common cause.

anna_cs: ACME said they have a short chat history saved on their side and they append it each call. They sent a redacted history and I forwarded it to Mohit.

jules_ml: Next steps: 1) Mohit tries to reproduce with the provided redacted history and streaming on. 2) Sam checks CDN/edge logs for any request mutation for rc-9f3a8b2e and for our canary instances. 3) Anna asks ACME to run non-streaming once and share the full raw response bytes if possible. 4) If we reproduce, we capture a heap/kcache snapshot and open a P0 bug.

mohit_eng: On it — ping me in-thread once Sam posts edge findings.

anna_cs: Will do. ACME appreciates the quick triage. I'll post updates here. :thumbsup:
